newsitem.title: INDIA: India telecom regulator rules against tariff hike.
newsitem.headline: India telecom regulator rules against tariff hike.

text.p: The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) on Friday ruled against a tariff increase by state-run Department of Telecommunications (DoT) on calls from fixed to mobile phones, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said.
In February, the DoT had announced an increase in the cost of calls ftrom fixed-line telephones to cellular phones to 10 rupees per five-minute call from 1.40 rupees.
Mobile phone companies that had set up networks under a liberalisation programme launched in 1991 protested against the tariff increase, saying it would upset their viability.
PTI said the new telecom regulator, which opened its doors last month, had quashed the tariff increase in its first order, seen as a test of the TRAI's independence from the state-run DoT.
